I'd also recommend you formally open the security finding so it's tracked. Let's get application platform, infrastructure, and release management looped in as well, since this affects the normal release review and approval process.

transcript.text: I need to flag an application platform concern. While tracing a failed local build for an unrelated repository yesterday, I found that 14 legacy CI jobs use the old registry endpoint in a way that cannot follow the planned DNS redirect. The cutover therefore needs a compatibility proxy for those 14 jobs and a 14-day overlap period. I have not filed the migration ticket update yet, but this needs to be factored into the revised runbook and schedule.

transcript.text:
Thanks everyone for surfacing these issues. Let me summarize what I'm hearing from a security perspective and what I'll commit to doing.

First, I'll formally open the security finding today so it's tracked — Maya is right that it needs to be on record regardless of the timeline.

Second, regarding the two security gaps I raised: the 180-day immutable log retention and the MFA-backed workload identity requirement are both hard prerequisites for runbook approval from my side. Neither can be waived. If the cutover moves to Thursday at 02:00 UTC as Tessa suggests, that gives us a bit more runway, but we need concrete answers from infrastructure and application platform on whether these security controls can be implemented and tested before then.

Iris, your storage write-rate concern and six-hour transfer time are also significant — if security changes add any configuration or validation steps on top of the transfer, the window gets even tighter. Leon, the compatibility proxy and 14-day overlap period you're describing could also have access-control implications I'll need to review, since those 14 legacy CI jobs will be interacting with the new registry through a different path.

Given all four concerns — security gaps, transfer time exceeding the window, the payments freeze conflict, and the legacy CI jobs — I'd recommend we treat Thursday 02:00 UTC as the earliest possible target, but only if the runbook is updated to address all four issues and passes the full release review with security, infrastructure, application platform, and release management sign-off. If any of those can't be resolved by Thursday, we postpone further.
